Motion system · draft 0.1 · for relationalsovereignty.com

BOTANICAL
MOTION SYSTEM

A pendant botanical layer for the site: how it grows, where it appears on each page, and what it is never allowed to do.

Three flora, one structure

Flor de Maga · Thespesia grandiflora Jade vine · Strongylodon macrobotrys Wisteria · W. floribunda

01 · Premise

Everything hangs.

Flor de Maga, jade vine, and wisteria share one structure: the raceme. A stem descends and buds hang off it in sequence, opening from the top down over days. Nothing on any of the three reaches upward.

That single fact settles most of the art direction. A climbing vine reads as ornament ascending a frame — Art Nouveau, wedding stationery, a border. A pendant raceme reads as weather: something that arrived, is hanging there, and will pass. It occupies the top and the margins, which is exactly where a text site has room.

The site's own constraints are the brief, not obstacles to it. A content security policy of script-src 'self' and a footer that promises exactly one third-party request rule out a CDN animation library. A hard contrast floor rules out anything drifting under body copy. A printable manifesto rules out a layer that has to be there for the page to make sense.

The result is a layer with no job. It carries no meaning, marks no state, and signals nothing. It breathes, and it gets out of the way.

02 · Visual language

Botanical illustration, not botanical decoration.

Everything is drawn as line first. Stems, pedicels, buds, and petals are strokes of 0.5–2.1px with round caps — the register of a hand-coloured engraving, held at a weight just above the paper's own texture. Under the line, each corolla carries a graded wash: dark at the throat, thinning toward the tips, capped at 0.36 before the layer's own opacity is applied, so a petal lands near 0.22 on paper. Nothing is ever drawn as a silhouette without its line. Nothing is blurred, nothing glows.

Structure

One dominant raceme per page. At most two faint echoes behind it at 40% of its opacity. Branching is sparse and alternate — never symmetrical, never a fan, never a tree diagram.

Line

Stem 1.7–2.1px, pedicel 1.1–1.35px, petal 1–1.15px, echo layers 0.7–1.05px. Every vine run takes its own thickening factor between 20% and 50%, applied to weight and to length together, so a group reads as several plants rather than one stroke repeated. Weight tapers with depth, never with length — a stem does not thin as it falls.

Colour

No new hues. The three bloom accents are saturated cousins of accents the site already uses — brick, sage, link blue. Each carries a throat tone and a tip tone derived from it, which is what lets a petal read as a petal. Vines run in a family of six greens rather than neutral ink, one shade held per run.

Density

A composition is capped at 14 blooms and 60 path nodes. If it needs more to read, the drawing is wrong, not too small.

03 · Motion grammar

Seven behaviours, all of them slow.

Every specimen below is live and running at the system's real timings. Nothing starts until it is scrolled into view, and nothing loops faster than forty seconds. Press replay to watch a growth cycle from the start.

{{ specRaceme }}

M1 · signature

Raceme descent

The stem draws downward over 22s and buds ride the tip as it goes. Nothing opens until the stem lands: after a settling beat the buds unfurl in sequence from the base down, one every dur × 0.5 ÷ count seconds, over 3.4s each. The whole cycle takes about 50 seconds and then simply stops, grown.

Use · once per page, on load, in the masthead or outer gutter. This is the only behaviour permitted to be noticed.

{{ specRhizome }}

M2 · connective

Rhizome run

A horizontal root travels the width of a section rule, throwing short branches and nodes as it goes. Ink only, no colour, no blooms. It reads as substrate, not subject.

Use · section boundaries and long lists. Replaces a hairline rule; never sits alongside one.

{{ specEmerge }}

M3 · scroll

Emergence

Growth begins when a composition crosses 35% into the viewport, and never reverses. Scrolling back up does not rewind it. Nothing is scrubbed to scroll position — the reader triggers growth, they do not drive it.

Use · every composition below the fold, without exception.

{{ specTendril }}

M4 · cursor

Tendril lean

Move the pointer across the panel. A tendril leans toward it by at most 8px over 1.2s of easing, and uncurls back when the pointer leaves. It follows late and arrives after you have stopped — that lag is the whole effect.

Use · at most one per viewport, near a card grid. Pointer devices only; never bound to touch or scroll.

{{ specGraft }}

M5 · composition

Inosculation

Two runners enter from opposite corners, grow toward each other at different rates, and fuse. The join is a single 2px node — the smallest mark in the system and the only one placed with any drama.

Use · pages built around meeting: Contribute, Invitation. Once per page, below the fold.

{{ specSway }}

M6 · ambient

Sway

Once grown, a composition never freezes. Each layer translates ±5px and rotates ±0.55° on its own 60–90s cycle, deliberately out of phase, so the group never returns to the same arrangement twice within a reading session.

Use · permanently, on every grown composition. The resting state of the entire system.

{{ specRetreat }}

M7 · deference

Retreat

Hover the panel. Growth withdraws toward its origin over 900ms and opacity halves. Any moment the reader needs to concentrate — a focused field, an open tool, a filter query — the layer recedes and stays back until they are done.

Use · Practise and Contribute, mandatory. Everywhere a form field takes focus.

Not in the grammar

Parallax. Scroll-scrubbed growth. Petals falling. Anything that spins, pulses on a beat, follows the cursor 1:1, or grows on hover. Each was drawn, tested, and cut — they read as toys, and this site is not one.

Also cut: blooms that open on click. Making the flower a reward for interaction turns an atmosphere into a slot machine.

05 · Tokens

Every number in one place

Ship these as one stylesheet. No component reads a raw value; if a timing needs to change it changes here, once. The three duration tokens are the only ones a designer should be adjusting after launch.

:root{
  /* line — multiplied per run by a 1.20–1.50 thickening factor */
  --bm-stem:      1.4px;   --bm-pedicel: 0.9px;
  --bm-petal:     1.05px;  --bm-hair:    0.42px;

  /* flora: hue / throat / tip */
  --bm-maga:      #A8374C; --bm-maga-deep: #6E1F31; --bm-maga-pale: #D4788C;
  --bm-jade:      #2E8F7E; --bm-jade-deep: #1B5C52; --bm-jade-pale: #79CDBC;
  --bm-wist:      #6C63A6; --bm-wist-deep: #443C78; --bm-wist-pale: #A79CD4;
  --bm-nectar:    #B98B36; /* wisteria guide only, never structural */

  /* stems — six greens, one held per run */
  --bm-green-1:#3D6B3A; --bm-green-2:#2F6B4E; --bm-green-3:#4A7040;
  --bm-green-4:#356043; --bm-green-5:#537A3C; --bm-green-6:#2C5A38;

  /* opacity ceilings */
  --bm-layer-signature: 0.55;  --bm-layer-support: 0.22;
  --bm-layer-ghost:     0.14;  --bm-wash-max:     0.36;

  /* time */
  --bm-grow:   20s;    /* stem draw, 8–30s by page      */
  --bm-settle: 2.2s;   /* pause after growth, before bloom */
  --bm-bloom:  3.4s;   /* one flower opening            */
  --bm-sway:   74s;    /* ambient cycle, 60–92s         */
  --bm-lean:   1.2s;   /* pointer response              */

  --bm-ease-grow:  cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1);
  --bm-ease-bloom: cubic-bezier(.18,.72,.3,1);
  --bm-ease-lean:  cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1);
}

Derived, not authored

bloom stagger

grow × 0.5 ÷ count. A slower stem blooms slower with no second number to tune.

bud birth

grow × t × 0.9, where t is the bud's position along the stem. Buds ride the drawing tip.

intensity

One page-level 1–10 scalar multiplies every opacity by n ÷ 6, capped. Geometry and timing never scale with it.

06 · Interaction

What it responds to

The layer is not a control surface. It answers to arrival and to the passage of time, and otherwise ignores the reader. Anything not listed here is a no.

Page load

Above-fold composition begins growing after a 300ms hold, so it starts under the reader's eye rather than mid-flight. Nothing below the fold is running.

Scroll

A composition starts once, at 35% into the viewport, and is unobserved immediately after. Scrolling back never rewinds or replays it. Scroll position is never mapped to growth progress.

Hover

Nothing. Links, cards, and buttons keep their existing states; no botanical element reacts to hovering content, and the layer itself is pointer-events:none.

Cursor

One tendril per viewport may lean toward the pointer, 8px maximum over 1.2s, and uncurl over 1.6s when it leaves. Never 1:1, never a follow. Written straight to a transform, outside the framework's render path.

Section change

A runner may cross a section rule and continue into the next block, but no composition animates because a section changed. Sections are not events.

Navigation

Each page grows once per visit, from nothing. No cross-page continuity, no transition choreography, no state persisted between loads. A returning reader sees it grow again.

Touch

M4 is omitted entirely below (hover:hover). Under 768px the layer drops to one composition per page, ghost layers removed, opacity ceiling 0.4, and it never sits behind body copy — only in the masthead and the page's outer edges.

Reduced motion

The site's existing prefers-reduced-motion rule already sets animation:none globally, which lands the layer fully grown and still — the intended fallback, not a degraded one. Every drawing must therefore be composed to look finished at rest.

Backgrounded tab

On visibilitychange to hidden, pause every running animation; resume on return. Sway must not burn cycles in a tab nobody is looking at.

Print

Hidden. @media print{.bm-layer{display:none}}

07 · Build

Three files, no dependencies

Everything here is inline SVG generated once at mount, animated by CSS. No canvas, no WebGL, no animation library. That is not a compromise: the drawing is a few hundred vector nodes with stroke-dashoffset on them, which CSS does on the compositor for free, and it keeps script-src 'self' intact and the footer's one-request promise honest.

assets/botanical/
  bm.css        tokens + keyframes + layer positioning   ~2 KB
  bm.js         geometry, species table, observer        ~7 KB
  bm-pages.js   one recipe per page                      ~1 KB

Markup contract

<!-- first child of a positioned ancestor; content sits above it -->
<div class="bm-layer" data-bm="home" aria-hidden="true"></div>

.bm-layer{position:absolute;inset:0;z-index:0;pointer-events:none;
          overflow:hidden;contain:layout paint}
.bm-layer > svg{display:block;width:100%;height:100%}

Recipe API

BM.register('home', {
  viewBox: [0, 0, 660, 600],
  intensity: 6,
  layers: [
    { type:'raceme', species:'maga', stem:[352,-24,468,118,296,250,344,588],
      count:7, alpha:.50, grow:20, settle:3.6, sway:78 },
    { type:'raceme', species:'maga', stem:[524,-30,566,140,452,244,486,470],
      count:4, alpha:.22, grow:26, delay:2.5, w:.8, sway:92, swayDelay:-20 },
    { type:'raceme', species:'maga', stem:[618,-14,668,160,594,268,626,452],
      count:3, alpha:.14, grow:30, delay:5,   w:.6, sway:66, swayDelay:-40 }
  ]
});

BM.init();  // finds every [data-bm], observes, mounts on first sight

Notes for the build

Stems are cubics

A stem is four points: [x0,y0,c1x,c1y,c2x,c2y,x1,y1]. Buds are placed by evaluating the curve at t, so composition changes need no hand-authored path data.

One gradient set per page

Petal washes reference six shared linearGradient defs in objectBoundingBox units. Emit them once per SVG; every petal in the document grades correctly off them.

Animate two properties

transform, opacity, plus stroke-dashoffset for growth. Nothing else. No filters, no blur, no blend modes, no will-change left on after growth.

Scaled transforms need a box

A keyframe transform replaces the SVG transform attribute rather than composing with it. Position on an outer <g>, animate an inner one, and set transform-box:fill-box — or the whole raceme collapses onto the origin.

Budget per page

≤ 3 SVGs, ≤ 3 stems each, ≤ 240 path nodes total, ≤ 1 pointer listener. If a composition needs more than that it is the wrong composition.

No-JS and no-CLS

The layer is absolutely positioned and empty until mounted, so a failed or blocked script costs nothing and shifts nothing. Never let the layer size a container.

08 · Restraint

Ten rules that keep it quiet

These are the load-bearing part of the system. The drawing survives being ignored; it does not survive being enthusiastically extended.

  1. One signature composition per page. If a second one is tempting, the first one is too weak.
  2. Never behind body copy above 0.2 opacity, and never behind a heading at all.
  3. No flower opens before its stem has finished drawing. Growth precedes bloom, always.
  4. Nothing loops faster than 60 seconds. Anything a reader can feel keeping time is out.
  5. The layer never indicates state. It is not a progress bar, a hover cue, a section marker, or a scroll indicator.
  6. No parallax, no scroll-scrubbed growth, no petals falling, no spin, no pulse, no cursor follow.
  7. Maximum three layers, and the back two never exceed a quarter of the front one's opacity.
  8. No blur, no glow, no drop shadow, no blend mode. Line and flat wash only.
  9. Growth happens once per page visit. Replay is a review affordance, not a feature.
  10. If it reads as decoration in a screenshot with the motion frozen, it is decoration. Cut it.

09 · Directions

Three ways this could have gone

All three were developed far enough to judge. The built system is B, holding A's line register and using C's runners as connective tissue between sections.

A · not taken

Pressed Herbarium

LookFlattened specimens, engraved line, pinned and labelled. Type and plant share one plane. SourceNineteenth-century botanical plates; the archive drawer. MotionAlmost none. A specimen fades up over 4s and holds. Archival, deliberate, still. VariationA different species per page, same plate treatment. VerdictCheapest to build and impossible to make feel alive. Without growth it is illustration, and illustration on a page about relations reads as wallpaper.

B · built

Pendant Raceme

LookStems descend from off the top edge; buds hang and open from the base down. Line first, graded wash under it. SourceFlor de Maga, jade vine, wisteria — three flora, one shared inflorescence. MotionSlow descent, a settling beat, then sequential opening. Patient, gravitational, never hurried. VariationSpecies, density, and permitted behaviours per page; the structure never changes. VerdictPendant, not climbing — which is what keeps it out of Art Nouveau border territory. Growth downward from the margin never crosses the reading column, so the one composition doing the most work is also the one least in the way.

C · partly absorbed

Substrate

LookNo flowers at all. A root and mycelial network runs beneath the whole document, surfacing at section rules. SourceRhizomes, fungal networks, the parts of a plant nobody photographs. MotionContinuous slow extension, no beginning or end. Subterranean, patient, faintly unsettling. VariationDensity and depth per page; one continuous organism across the site. VerdictConceptually the strongest and the easiest to mistake for a network-graph background. Alone it also forfeits colour entirely. Kept as M2 and M5, where connective tissue is the actual job.

10 · Sign-off

Done means all of these

No flower is mid-open while its stem is still drawing, on any page, at any viewport.

With prefers-reduced-motion set, every composition renders complete, still, and correct — no partial stems, no invisible blooms.

Body copy contrast is unchanged with the layer on. Measured, not eyeballed.

Every SVG is aria-hidden, unfocusable, and absent from the tab order and the accessibility tree.

Sustained 60fps during growth on a mid-range Android; no layout thrash, no CLS attributable to the layer.

Below 768px: one composition, no pointer behaviours, nothing behind text.

Script blocked or failed: page is visually intact and unshifted.

CSP unchanged, and the site still makes exactly one third-party request.
